issue.body:
Part of #665 (Mark II split). Owner request 2026-11-10: bring up the split image on the Arty A7-100T, beside the AX7101's release bench. Depends on S9 (#870), whose builder recipe makes split images. Relates to #583 (Arty configurations) and #829 (gPTP on MII).

**Scope.**
- One Arty configuration with `control.placement: split` at the 1x1 shape, through S9's recipe. 100 Mb/s MII carries 1x1, not 8x8.
- DDR3 is left out, as on every split image (decision D4). The system clock is set without DDR3's 83.333 MHz window, and the choice is stated.
- The build-time latency pair keeps the board's calibration; any bench compensation is written at runtime only and never tracked.
- A defect found on the board is fixed here only if it is small and has a regression test that fails without it; otherwise it gets its own issue.

**Acceptance.**
1. **Build.**
   - S9's identity gate passes on the Arty manifest.
   - The split simulation boots to ready.
   - Routed WNS and WHS are at or above 0 at every corner, recorded against the +0.030 ns floor. A bench image, not a release image.
   - LUT, FF and BRAM are reported.
2. **Boot.**
   - The firmware reaches ready on the UART.
   - The ident string names the split placement, and the mailbox `ID` register reads the contract version.
3. **Link and enumeration.**
   - Link at 100 Mb/s.
   - The controller enumerates the entity.
   - Every descriptor is byte-identical to the all-fabric Arty image's, or each difference is explained against IEEE 1722.1-2021 and Milan v1.2.
4. **gPTP.**
   - asCapable and sync to the bench grandmaster (IEEE 802.1AS-2020 10.2, 11.2), with offset and peer delay recorded over at least 10 minutes.
   - Any runtime compensation is stated beside each figure.
5. **Streams** (Milan v1.2 5.5; IEEE 802.1Q-2022 35).
   - One talker and one listener connection with the reference peer.
   - Every stream counter is read.
   - Frames are checked on the capture.
6. **Soak.** One hour with both connections up, every counter recorded before and after, and no discontinuity.
7. **Save.** One descriptor change saved and read back after a reset, with the save time measured. The measurement feeds #876's model (save time proportional to the data saved). The Arty's flash differs from the AX7101's, so the figure is the Arty's own.

**Out of scope.**
- 8x8.
- Power cycles: the Arty has no remote power control.
- S12 (the AX7101 split bench) and the flip (S13).

decisions.body:
[A10] Ruling on the round-1 STOP: **option 1**. The Arty keeps its entity shape: AAF talker, AAF listener, CRF input. That already meets Milan v1.2 7.2.2, and a CRF output is only required with two AAF inputs (7.2.3). Option 2 would change the model identity (IEEE 1722.1-2021 6.2.2.8) and still need the same clock evidence.

Next round:
- Add a (1 interface, 1 source, 2 sinks) point at 83,333,000 Hz to the service-budget harness. Measure it and derive its row by the existing rules.
- If any bound fails (load 0.70, txL 49 ms, THE SHARE 2 ms, last notice 140 ms, ACMP 30 ms), STOP.
- Advertise 100BASE-TX full duplex only (IEEE 802.1BA-2011 Table 6-1 and 6.5, through Milan v1.2 4.2.1), gated to the MII platform.
- AX7101 1x1/8x8 images byte-identical.
- Best-of-three routes at four corners against the #818 floor.
- Then bench: boot, enumeration, a 100 Mb/s full-duplex link and one stream each way.

[A10] Ruling on the round-2 STOP: my round-2 ruling carried the YAML's 83,333,000 Hz. The production CRG needs an exact divider (`margin=0`), and the 100 MHz oscillator cannot give that rate. The Arty's sys/CPU clock becomes **80,000,000 Hz exactly**: a VCO of 800 MHz divided by 10, with 50 / 25 / 200 MHz at /16, /32 and /4. That keeps the exact-divider contract and an integer clock, so no nominal/actual mapping is needed. The datapath stays at 50 MHz.

At 80 MHz the bootstrap's longest pass (132,507 cycles) is about 1.66 ms, inside THE SHARE. The (1,1,2) point is measured and derived at 80 MHz. Every other part of the round-2 instruction is unchanged, including STOP if an owner bound fails.

[A10] Ruling on the round-3 STOP: the seven held-egress rows are `backlog-owed`'s rows, set by the scenario's 60 ms egress hold. No CPU lever moves them, and they miss at every point, the AX7101's included. #894's held-egress ruling ([item (a)](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/894#issuecomment-6871343905)) puts them in `egress_ledger.py` as recorded misses: FR_NFR 3.4.1 still charges the backpressure, and a new or larger miss fails.

The Arty gets its own ledger rows, derived by the same rule at its point: HOLD_MS + the service measured at 80 MHz, by the ledger's own procedure, with the ledger self-test extended to the new rows. This is the existing rule applied to a new point, not a waiver. My round-3 "never waived" line was wrong for these rows.

Round 4 implements the whole round-2 instruction at 80 MHz. It STOPs only if an owner bound fails (load 0.70, txL 49 ms, THE SHARE 2 ms, last notice 140 ms, ACMP 30 ms) or if a row other than the seven misses.

[A10] Ruling on the acceptance of #878 for the 80 MHz Arty split image (PR #1004), decided under the owner's delegation.

**Item 5, "frames are checked on the capture": a ruled deviation, not met as written.**
- **Reason.** The owner removed the in-line tap on 2026-11-24 and set "no tap" for the Arty bench. No Linux host sits on the stream path to capture from (bench report round 2 on #1004).
- **Substitute evidence, accepted:** every stream counter at both ends over the 3,683 s soak (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.42). The counters are MEDIA_LOCKED 1, MEDIA_UNLOCKED 0, STREAM_INTERRUPTED 0, SEQ_NUM_MISMATCH 0, MEDIA_RESET 0, TIMESTAMP_UNCERTAIN 0, TIMESTAMP_NOT_VALID 0, UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT 0, LATE 0 and EARLY 0. All were unchanged at all 29 reads, and the frame counts match end to end (board TX +29,463,421 = peer RX +29,463,420; peer TX +29,463,321 = board TS_VALID +29,463,320; CRF equal).
- **Independent check.** The reference peer's own parser accepted 29.46 M frames.

**Item 4: peer delay and sync/asCapable are met; the offset is not.**
- Met: peer delay every 5 s for an hour, and sync with asCapable at every poll.
- Not met: a bound of [-12.10, +0.29] ms on the offset is not a record. #878 stays open on that single line, which closes with #1007's criterion 4 run on the Arty.

**Items 6 and 7: met.** The 1-hour soak and the save read back after a reset (1.15 to 1.25 s for a 2,600 B container).

**PR #1004** relates to #878 rather than closing it, and may merge on its own gates.

registration_decisions.body:
[A10] Ruling on the round-2 STOP (owner-delegated decision, 2026-11-22): **option 1**.
- **Why option 1:** #969 is a lab-visible failure on every input. Its kept records are cheaper than the bound records the base already makes on any bridged network, so it adds no new worst case.
- **Why not the others:** option 3 reintroduces the failure for the refused Talkers. Option 2 is a registration redesign, too risky this close to the lab.

**Conditions for REVIEW READY:**
- commit the bound group beside `srp-kept`;
- grade both as owed to #977, the registration cost, held at kept <= bound on the same image and no pass over THE SHARE;
- do not restate the SRP unit.

The registration cost itself is tracked and fixed in #977 on the product shapes, before the post-flip in-house qualification is closed.

[A10] Ruling on the composition's STOP at 8x8/1if (owner-delegated decision, 2026-11-23), amending the conditions of issuecomment-7083542634.

**What the composed image measures (formal CPU budget, every arm and group):**
- **kept <= bound, arm A:** the kept Failed record is 142,582 CPU cycles against the bound record's 142,137, over by 445 (0.31 %).
  - The kept path did not grow: 142,909 at this issue's head, 142,582 composed.
  - The bound record became about 11,000 cycles cheaper in the composition: 153,208 down to 142,137.
- **Bound path, answering-ports:** `srp-bound`'s build of one MRPDU takes 171,645 cycles against `CTRL_LOOP_BUILD_ONE_PASS_US` (147,500).
- **Bound path, THE SHARE:** one `srp-bound` work pass of 216,785 cycles is over THE SHARE.
- **The kept path stays inside:** 0 passes over THE SHARE, and a build of one at 81,655.

**Ruling:**
1. **kept <= bound** is held within the established measurement rule (#665 ruling item 4: measurement + 5 %) on the same image. 142,582 <= 142,137 x 1.05 holds.
   - The condition exists to show the kept records add no new worst case.
   - A composition that makes the bound side cheaper does not change that.
   - It is still graded on every image.
2. **The bound path's build-of-one pass and its pass over THE SHARE are the registration cost #977 owns.**
   - #977's ruling requires THE SHARE and the build slice to hold, round 2 by 11-25.
   - They are graded OWED to #977, not raised. `CTRL_LOOP_BUILD_ONE_PASS_US` and the SRP unit are not restated.
   - #977 must clear both on the composed head before the post-flip in-house qualification closes.
3. **Every owner bound holds at the composed head:**
   - loads 0.512 / 0.744 of 0.70 / 0.75;
   - last notice 127.43 ms;
   - ACMP 29.15 ms;
   - txL 47.98 ms;
   - THE TRANSMIT 76.86 ms.
   The composition proceeds to review.

registration_debt.body:
## Scope

PR #1004 (#878) qualifies the Arty split image at its installed row (slice 1250 us, AECP pace 10 ms): load 0.5005, ACMP 29.77 ms, txL 48.82 ms, last notice 117.47 ms, longest pass 1.785 ms.

The qualification applies #969's disposition (ruling of 2026-11-23, issuecomment-7116192252, item 2): the `srp-kept` and `srp-bound` SRP records are left out of the derivation as registration cost owed. These are records up to 495 us and one build of 740 us. #977 owns that cost at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, but its acceptance does not name the Arty point. This issue carries it there, so the owed lines have an owner (internal review of PR #1004, finding F1, comment 7210534024).

## Acceptance

- Measure the registration cost at the Arty point (`arty-1x1`, 4x4/1if target) on the composed head after #977 lands, with the method #977 uses at the other points.
- Derive the Arty row with those records counted, by the rule and with no hand tuning. Qualify it against the owner bounds: load 0.70, ACMP 30 ms, txL 49 ms, last notice 140 ms, THE SHARE 2 ms.
- Publish the derivation without the disposition, as the control. The author's figure is a last notice of about 225 ms.
- Close only when the Arty's census has no `owed_969` exclusion left, or a public decision records how each remaining line is discharged.

Relates to #878, #969, #977. Blocked by #977.
